'''EPP Overdrive''' is a fast Star Wars CCG sealed-deck format: each player opens one [[Enhanced Premiere]] pack, builds a 30-card deck, and plays 15-minute games. [[Decipher]] introduced it in 1999 as "the newest sanctioned Sealed Deck tournament format".<ref name="epp99">[http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/epptournaments/index.html EPP Overdrive], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991010234206/http://decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/epptournaments/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Type:''' sealed deck
* '''Defined by:''' Decipher (1999)
* '''Card pool:''' one Enhanced Premiere pack per player; 30-card decks
* '''In use:''' 1999 –
* '''Also called:''' EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck Format (Decipher, 2001–2002)<ref name="epp02">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/eppoverdriveformat.asp EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck Format], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020220230930/http://tournaments.decipher.com/eppoverdriveformat.asp Internet Archive].</ref>
* '''GEMP:''' none

== Card pool ==
Decipher's rules:<ref name="epp99" />
* '''Product:''' "each player starts with one Enhanced Premiere Pack. It is highly recommended that the players use Vader with Lightsaber EPP to build Dark Side decks and Luke with Lightsaber EPP to build Light Side decks", though any pack of the right side works. Directors provide equal numbers of Dark and Light packs.
* '''Deck building:''' 15 minutes, strictly timed. Opponents of opposite sides open their packs and give each other, face down, the cards of the other side; each player then builds "their own deck of 30 cards". Between games a player may tweak the deck only with cards left over from their own pack.
* '''Games:''' a 15-minute limit, strictly enforced; a game over time is scored as a modified win (1 victory point plus the winner's Life Force as differential).
* '''Event:''' the standard minimum for sanctioned sealed deck of 3 games, but "it is preferable to run between 4 and 6 games." Byes score 2 victory points and 0 differential.

Decipher pitched it as "a fast-moving alternative to the typical four-hour event".<ref name="epp99" /> The recommended packs contain [[Darth Vader With Lightsaber]] and [[Luke With Lightsaber]].

== History ==
Decipher's EPP Overdrive page, with links for directors to post events and players to find them, was online by October 1999.<ref name="epp99" /> At [[DecipherCon 1999]] the Star Wars schedule held EPP Overdrive (SW.24) on Thursday 11 November, 11 p.m.–3 a.m., and Saturday 13 November, 5–9 p.m.<ref name="dc99-thu">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/thu_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule (Thursday)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122035723/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/thu_events.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="dc99-sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sat_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule (Saturday)], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026023004/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sat_events.html Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher's 2001–2002 tournament site still listed the "EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck Format" with the same rules.<ref name="res-sw">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/resources-sw.asp Star Wars Customizable Card Game Tournament Resources], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011116144130/http://tournaments.decipher.com/resources-sw.asp Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="epp02" />

The Players Committee's Alternate Format Tournament Guide keeps EPP Overdrive: one Enhanced Premiere Pack, 30-card decks, 15-minute games, 15 minutes of deck building, and a minimum of 4 games.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>
